solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Hit by a lot of commotion, tip for your uplifting narrative (7,5)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of STORM, not all of it, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.tip for: the tip of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone battered by chaos offers advice for making your own story upbeat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like a verb, someone struck amid the commotion, but it is the noun: a hit is a success.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a story of someone overcoming the odds is told to lift the listener.

entries.clue: Questionable party skirting distinctive feature (7)

indicatorNotes.skirting: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so SECT goes round USP

blocks.note: a sect = a faction or party

annotation.surface: A dubious gathering gives a wide berth to anything that stands out.
annotation.walkthrough: USP, the marketing 'unique selling point', is the distinctive feature that a product boasts of.
annotation.definitionFit: Something suspect is open to doubt: questionable.

entries.clue: Shellfish left in river attracting punters (4)

indicatorNotes.in: L goes inside the river's name

blocks.note: the Cam, the Cambridge river famous for punting

annotation.surface: A shellfish left in a river that draws in people with punts.
annotation.walkthrough: Punters look like gamblers; here they are people steering punts, flat boats poled along the Cam at Cambridge.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the clam is one kind of shellfish among many.

entries.clue: Government entering housing agreement (7)

indicatorNotes.housing: the phrase houses the answer within its letters

annotation.surface: The state moves into the business of providing homes, by agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Government' and 'entering' look like a container instruction, but they are merely the two words the answer straddles.
annotation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, an agreement.

entries.clue: Cave in America’s raised volume, huge internally (7)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word writes it bottom to top
indicatorNotes.internally: only the inside of JUMBO is used

blocks.note: cc = cubic centimetres, a measure of volume

annotation.surface: In America the volume is turned up, enormous on the inside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cave' looks like a noun, a hollow in America; with 'in' it is the verb phrase meaning give way.
annotation.definitionFit: To succumb is to give way under pressure, to cave in.

entries.clue: Wind in Italy absent from one of its cities? (4)

indicatorNotes.absent from: I is missing from the city's name

blocks.note: I = Italy, its international vehicle code; removed

annotation.surface: A question about a breeze across Italy that never reaches one of its towns.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the breeze, but it is the verb that rhymes with 'find': to wind a road is to turn it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: a road that winds keeps bending this way and that.

entries.clue: Discharged rifle certain to backfire (7)

indicatorNotes.Discharged: a word discharged of its contents keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: bound = certain, as in 'bound to happen'

annotation.surface: A gun that has been fired is sure to go wrong on its user.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' plays on a rifle being fired, when it asks for the rifle's contents to be discharged, leaving only R and E.
annotation.definitionFit: To rebound is to spring back on the person responsible, to backfire.

entries.clue: Fanatical members in a cult sporting hair on face (7,6)

indicatorNotes.sporting: sporting suggests the letters playing about, mixed up

blocks.note: a fringe is hair hanging over the forehead

annotation.surface: Zealots in a sect show off their beards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' pairs with 'hair on face' as if the cultists wear beards; it is the mixing instruction for the three words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: The lunatic fringe is the most extreme members of a group, its fanatics.

entries.clue: Pass a critical point of recent Roth novel about pot (4,3,6)

indicatorNotes.novel: novel means new, so the letters are made new
indicatorNotes.about: the jumbled letters go around URN

blocks.note: an urn is a pot; placed after the first T

annotation.surface: A reviewer calls the latest Philip Roth book, about cannabis, a turning point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'pot' both lure the reader into a literary review about drugs; 'novel' is the mixing instruction and the pot is a vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: To turn the corner is to get past the crisis point, as a patient does in recovery.

entries.clue: Social climber‘s finished with graffiti? (7)

blocks.note: graffiti is street art: ST (street) + ART

annotation.surface: An ambitious newcomer is done for, caught spray-painting.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that graffiti is being described rather than defined: it is street art, with street shortened to its usual ST.
annotation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly in status and acts above it, a social climber.

entries.clue: Heard expression of disgust by wife of former prime minister, big beast (7)

indicatorNotes.Heard: the answer is what you hear when the two pieces are said

blocks.note: Carrie Johnson, wife of Boris Johnson

annotation.surface: A former PM's wife is heard jeering a hulking creature.
annotation.walkthrough: Carrie Johnson is the wife of Boris Johnson, UK prime minister 2019-22. Only the sound matters: CARRIE BOO spoken is CARIBOU.
annotation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large deer.

entries.clue: Gets older wife to leave reward (4)

indicatorNotes.to leave: W leaves the word, so it is removed

annotation.surface: An older wife is asked to walk away from her payoff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets older wife' reads as one phrase about a husband's new partner; the break comes after 'older'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean growing old, and 'gets' matches the third-person S.

entries.clue: Scrap is yearly bar brawl essentially (5)

indicatorNotes.bar: bar = except, so A is left out
indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its middle

annotation.surface: A fight is the annual event at the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar brawl' is the pub fight the surface wants; 'bar' is really 'except'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a court scraps a marriage or contract by declaring it void.

entries.clue: Break hip at end of game (4)

indicatorNotes.at end of: read literally, the hip sits at the end of the game, so IN comes after RU

annotation.surface: Someone fractures a hip as the match ends.
annotation.walkthrough: The hip looks like a body part broken in the game; it means trendy, which is IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to wreck or destroy.

entries.clue: Case for routinely bolstering dog food (5)

indicatorNotes.Case for: the case of a word is its outside letters
indicatorNotes.bolstering: in a down clue, RY goes underneath CUR to support it

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: An argument for regularly beefing up a dog's diet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case for' looks like the start of an argument; it asks for the case, the outside, of 'routinely'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the spiced dish is one example of food.

entries.clue: Wicket and dodgy shot at cricket club (5)

blocks.note: an edge is a shot off the side of the bat

annotation.surface: A cricket club notes a wicket falling to a streaky shot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cricket club' reads as one unit; the club is golf's, a wedge, and 'at cricket' belongs to the shot.
annotation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club with a steep face for lofted shots.

entries.clue: Interfere with focus of Liverpool – to stop United playing (7)

indicatorNotes.focus of: the focus is the centre, the middle letter
indicatorNotes.to stop: R plugs the gap inside the other letters

blocks.note: middle letter of LiveRpool, placed after INT

annotation.surface: Liverpool try to prevent Manchester United from getting a game going.
annotation.walkthrough: The football surface puts Liverpool and United on the pitch; each only lends letters, one from the middle of Liverpool and all of UNITED mixed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean pushing in where you are not wanted.

entries.clue: Measure elder’s heart murmur to check (7)

indicatorNotes.heart: the heart of a word is its middle letter
indicatorNotes.to check: BREATH holds D back, containing it

blocks.note: a breath = a whisper, a murmur

annotation.surface: A doctor listens to an old person's heart murmur.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heart murmur' is the medical phrase the surface builds; split, 'heart' belongs to 'elder's' and 'murmur' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Breadth is a dimension, a measure of how wide something is.

entries.clue: Plot to banish leading character in wild system of government (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the plot ends up in the wild, so ED sits inside FERAL

annotation.definitionNote: FEDERAL is an adjective; the definition names the system it describes

blocks.note: a bed is a garden plot
BED without B; placed after the F of FERAL

annotation.surface: Conspirators try to exile the main figure from an untamed regime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a conspiracy; it is a flower bed. The pieces go F(ED)ERAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A federal system is one of government by a union of states under a central power.

entries.clue: Gent with a doc wasting time, fabulously in shape (7)

indicatorNotes.wasting: to waste time is to let it go, so T is thrown away
indicatorNotes.fabulously: treated fabulously, as in a fable, the letters are made up anew

annotation.surface: A man and his doctor are idling away, in marvellous physical condition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In shape' reads as fit and healthy; 'in' is the link and the shape is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the ten-sided polygon is one example of a shape.

entries.clue: Well-read Listener buried in large study turned up (7)

indicatorNotes.buried in: EAR is buried inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning a word up writes it bottom to top

annotation.surface: An erudite eavesdropper hides in a big study that has been flipped over.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital on Listener suggests the magazine or a named person; it is simply an ear.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, said as two syllables (LEARN-ED): scholarly from much reading.

entries.clue: Natural skin, say, nice unclothed (7)

indicatorNotes.say: skin is an example of an organ
indicatorNotes.unclothed: a word unclothed loses its outer letters

blocks.note: the skin is the body's largest organ

annotation.surface: Bare skin, someone says, is pleasantly natural.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about nudity; 'unclothed' strips the word 'nice', not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown naturally, without artificial chemicals.

entries.clue: Put down hole with Poulter’s number one iron (7)

indicatorNotes.number one: the first letter of the name

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them

annotation.surface: The golfer Ian Poulter holes out using his favourite iron.
annotation.walkthrough: Ian Poulter is an English golfer, so 'hole', 'iron' and 'Put' all sound like golf; the iron is for clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: To oppress people is to keep them down by force: to put them down.

entries.clue: Developing US stock exchange down by half, little money there (7)

blocks.clueFragment: US stock exchange down by half

blocks.note: a cent is a small coin in the US, 'there'

annotation.surface: Wall Street shares have halved in value, leaving hardly any cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to the US: the cent is that country's small coin.
annotation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, developing.

entries.clue: Creep from Squeeze knocking off piano (4)

indicatorNotes.knocking off: P is knocked off the front

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music; removed

annotation.surface: The band Squeeze lose their keyboard player, and someone sneaks away.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S and 'piano' suggest the band Squeeze and its keyboards; it is just the verb pinch, less the musical P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: moving forward a tiny distance at a time.

entries.clue: Twists in lounge abruptly turning (5)

indicatorNotes.abruptly: cut short, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.turning: turning round faces the word the other way, so it reads backwards

annotation.surface: Someone lolling about suddenly rolls over and contorts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room; it is the verb, to sprawl.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: damp timber bends out of true.

entries.clue: Customer with cunning manoeuvre first to finish (4)

indicatorNotes.first to finish: the first letter moves to the finish

blocks.note: RUSE (a crafty trick), left behind when its first letter moves on
the R from the front of RUSE, now at the end

annotation.surface: A shopper with a crafty plan to get to the checkout first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First to finish' reads as winning a race; it tells the first letter to go to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in business speak: the people buying a service are its customers.

entries.clue: Section of song, energy to knock out one? (4)

indicatorNotes.to knock out: E knocks out one letter and takes its place

blocks.note: an aria is an operatic song
I = one, the Roman numeral; knocked out

annotation.surface: A section of a song has enough energy to floor someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Section of song' looks like the definition; the definition is just 'Section', and 'of' belongs to the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a part marked off from the whole, as a section of a field.

entries.clue: Picked up pen, problem with lid (4)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: picked up by the ear, heard

annotation.surface: Someone grabs a pen, then struggles to get the cap off.
annotation.walkthrough: The lid is an eyelid, not a pen top, and the pen is a pig's enclosure, not for writing.
annotation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid.

entries.clue: Lady who sings right at home producing Rocket Man (7)

annotation.surface: Lady Gaga, relaxing at home, puts out a cover of Elton John's Rocket Man.
annotation.walkthrough: Rocket Man is an Elton John song, so the music surface holds together; here it is Yuri Gagarin, the first man in space.
annotation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin rode a rocket into orbit in 1961, the first man in space.

entries.clue: Ultimate in messages uncovered about short guys (7)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: a word uncovered loses its outer letters
indicatorNotes.short: MEN falls short of its last letter

blocks.note: tEXTs, text messages, without the outer letters

annotation.surface: The last word in messages exposed about small men.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Messages' must first become TEXTS before it can be uncovered; 'short guys' looks like a remark on height.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: the furthest possible, as in extreme or ultimate sacrifice.

entries.clue: Red-hot in May, son visiting fair (12)

indicatorNotes.visiting: S goes to stay inside DECENT

blocks.note: S = son; goes inside DECENT after DE

annotation.surface: A scorching May, with a son going to a fair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month, and so 'in May' like a date; it is the verb, can. The pieces run IN + CAN + DE(S)CENT.
annotation.definitionFit: Something incandescent glows with heat, red-hot.
